hero.headline: AI tools are enabling automated hacking at scale, upending the cybersecurity industry
hero.body:
Artificial intelligence systems are now enabling attackers to automate the entire hacking process in real time, fundamentally disrupting the cybersecurity industry built over the past two decades, according to Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and a longtime cybersecurity expert. Open-weight AI models have advanced to the point where they can automatically identify software vulnerabilities, write exploits, and break into targets simultaneously, collapsing what was traditionally a multi-step process requiring teams of skilled hackers.

Stamos described a wave of breaches in recent weeks affecting major technology companies, including a chain of attacks that began with a compromise of Fireworks, an AI services provider. Attackers stole API keys from Fireworks that enabled them to breach Cursor, a code editor, where they pushed a malicious plugin to 5,000 additional companies, creating what Stamos called a "permanent continuous breach" across the tech industry. He also cited the Binance hack, which he characterized as the largest heist in history, and attacks on roughly 200 companies using ARTEX, a Chinese open-source hacking tool that anyone can download.

The shift eliminates barriers that previously limited cyberattacks. Where breaking into systems once required rare technical expertise and large teams, now attackers can use locally run AI models on consumer hardware to conduct sophisticated operations. Stamos said he has been running an AI model on an Apple Mac Studio that can reverse engineer software patches and write exploit code, capabilities that previously belonged only to elite hackers. Both criminal groups and state actors in countries including Russia, China, and North Korea are deploying these AI-powered tools.

Stamos compared the current moment to the 1990s, when the internet was new and security practices were still being developed, calling it a return to "Wild West days." The multibillion-dollar cybersecurity industry that emerged in the 2000s and 2010s was built on assumptions about skill hierarchies and operational structures that AI has now rendered obsolete. While Stamos said he is not pessimistic long-term, he believes the industry faces a "dark age" as it struggles to adapt to automated, AI-enabled attacks.
}

cards.headline: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear program
cards.teaser: State Department launches rewards program as military establishes new task force targeting weapons smuggling.
cards.body:
The United States announced a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear program, including details on facilities, equipment, and personnel. The State Department said Iran's lack of compliance with the International Atomic Energy Agency has caused a loss of knowledge regarding production and inventory of components such as centrifuges, which are used to enrich uranium.

Separately, the U.S. military's Central Command said it is establishing Task Force Iron Gate to restrict Iran's movement of weapons and sanctioned material across its borders. The task force, which will operate from Tampa, Florida, will also focus on dual-use items and illegal revenue streams. Centcom estimates its naval blockade has prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil.

cards.headline: Secret Service arrests man near White House with guns who said voices told him to kill Trump
cards.teaser: The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice
cards.body:
The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

Officers approached Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos after observing him acting suspiciously in a parked car, according to a Department of Homeland Security statement. Chrinos described hearing voices instructing him to come to Washington and kill the president, the statement said.

cards.headline: Congress demands answers on Nvidia CEO's reported ties to alleged Chinese spy
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing congressional scrutiny after reports surfaced that he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Sen. Chris Coons pledged an investigation, while a group of House Republican committee chairs requested a briefing from Huang by November 11 to determine whether U.S. national security has been compromised.

Multiple news outlets reported Friday that Alice Huang, a tech executive with whom Jensen Huang had contact, was recruited by Chinese intelligence officials to influence the Nvidia CEO's position on U.S. chip export policy toward China. The New York Times and Financial Times reported she was specifically tasked with convincing him to lobby U.S. officials to allow exports of advanced chips to China. The Financial Times also reported that the two had a romantic relationship.

Nvidia has denied that Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang was anything beyond a typical business contact and said no sensitive information was shared. The Chinese government has also denied involvement. The company did not respond to a request for comment Saturday.

The House Republican chairs who requested the briefing asked Huang to explain his relationship with Alice Huang and detail Nvidia's controls over sensitive information. Nvidia produces chips central to advanced artificial intelligence development, a technology priority for the Trump administration as it seeks to maintain a competitive edge over China. Reports indicate Nvidia chips have reached Chinese companies despite export restrictions.

cards.headline: Treasury moves to cut crypto exchange MEXC from U.S. financial system over alleged $16 billion in illicit transactions
cards.teaser: The action targets alleged ties to Iran, North Korea, and Russia.
cards.body:
The U.S. Treasury Department is moving to sever cryptocurrency exchange MEXC from the American financial system over allegations the platform processed $16 billion in illicit transactions. The action targets alleged dealings linked to Iran, North Korea, and Russia.

The Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network is blocking MEXC's access to U.S. financial infrastructure over alleged sanctions evasion. The enforcement action has already prompted at least one cryptocurrency issuer to announce the immediate delisting of its token from the exchange.

cards.teaser: Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk said Friday. Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the
cards.body:
Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk said Friday. Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the

Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the trucks entirely or shift production elsewhere, but said the decision was to make room for building more of its self-driving Cybercab cars. Wes Morrill, the project's lead engineer, wrote on social media that Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab, appearing to suggest the vehicle is being discontinued.

hero.headline: Gunman kills six in attack on Krakow's main square, three more bodies found at his home
hero.body:
At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman opened fire in central Krakow on Saturday afternoon, and police later found three bodies at his home. The attacker, identified as a 25-year-old Polish man, drove into Krakow's Main Market Square shortly before 15:00 local time and began firing at random people from his car. Armed officers shot and arrested him within three minutes, preventing further casualties. A minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by far-right ideologies and described him as an ultra-nationalist.

The six confirmed dead include four women and two men, among them a British national. Three victims are Polish and two have not been identified. Sixteen people were taken to hospital, including five foreigners and the attacker. Two police officers were shot while detaining the gunman, one described as being in very critical condition after being shot three times. When authorities searched the suspect's home, they found three bodies, two women and one man.

The attacker was wearing military-style attire and had a military-grade weapon, though authorities confirmed he was not a soldier. Police found multiple pieces of weapons and ammunition in his vehicle. Polish media reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home. Counter-terrorism police are supporting the search of his residence.

The shooting occurred in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a popular tourist destination. Witnesses described hearing more than 20 shots from what sounded like multiple different firearms. A passing tram was shot at during the attack, shattering windows, though no passengers were injured. Prime Minister Donald Tusk traveled to Krakow and said Poland had not previously experienced such drastic cases of terrorism. Krakow Mayor Åukasz GibaÅa declared a period of mourning in the city lasting until Wednesday.

cards.headline: Israel's president taps Gadi Eisenkot to form next government
cards.teaser: Former army chief has 28 days to build a coalition after securing more lawmaker endorsements than Benjamin Netanyahu.
cards.body:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country's next government, passing over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Herzog announced the decision Saturday after consultations with political parties following the October 27 general election, in which neither side secured a majority. Some 67 lawmakers endorsed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, while 46 backed Netanyahu.

Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to build a coalition of at least 61 of the Knesset's 120 seats. His four-party alliance won 48 seats in the election, while Netanyahu's bloc secured 53. If Eisenkot fails to form a government, Herzog will nominate another candidate. Eisenkot led Israel's military from 2015 to 2019.

cards.headline: Paraguay formally charges ousted president Santiago Peña over bank collapse
cards.teaser: Prosecutors charge former president with breach of trust after impeachment over banking scandal that left millions unable to access savings.
cards.body:
Prosecutors in Paraguay have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain following his impeachment over a banking scandal. Peña was removed from office Friday after the collapse of Ueno Bank left more than half the country's population unable to access their savings and pensions.

Peña, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, denies any wrongdoing. His defense lawyer described the charges as reckless and opportunistic. Lawmakers unanimously impeached Peña rather than accept his resignation, stripping him of the immunity typically granted to former presidents. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and pledged full compensation for affected citizens.

hero.headline: Wisconsin state trooper detained by ICE released under supervision after intervention by DHS secretary
hero.body:
A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an airport Thursday while attempting to visit his parents. Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision following intervention by Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, according to his attorney.

Van Der Merwe entered the United States in 2019 at age 14 and attended high school in New Mexico, according to attorney Mark Christopher. His parents applied for asylum, and Van Der Merwe was granted work authorization while that process proceeded. He later attended the New Mexico Military Institute and sought to serve in the U.S. military but was not permitted because of his immigration status. Van Der Merwe began working as a Wisconsin state trooper in July 2025 and remains authorized to work in the country, Christopher said.

The Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that Van Der Merwe had legal permission to remain in the United States until September 2019 but overstayed his admission. The agency characterized the overstay as defiance of federal immigration law.

Christopher said the case was egregious and that he could not identify any public benefit from detaining Van Der Merwe. The trooper will remain under an order of supervision, with specific conditions to be determined within two weeks, according to his attorney.

cards.headline: Six killed in shooting in Krakow, Poland; British national among victims
cards.teaser: A gunman opened fire in a busy tourist square in Poland's second-largest city, killing six and injuring more than a dozen others.
cards.body:
A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others Saturday afternoon in Krakow's Main Market Square, a popular tourist attraction in Poland's second-largest city. The attacker, a 25-year-old Polish man equipped with military-style weapons, drove through the square firing at people before being injured in a gunfight with police. Four women and two men died in the square, including one British national and three Polish citizens.

Polish authorities said the suspect held far-right and ultra-nationalist views. Three additional bodies, believed to be the suspect's immediate family members, were found during a search of his home about 125 miles from Krakow. Two police officers were injured during the confrontation, one critically. Poland's prime minister called the attack an act of terrorism.

cards.headline: Actress Ambika Mod says glass ceiling for South Asian actors 'always getting higher'
cards.teaser: The British actress, who stars in the second season of Black Doves, says systemic racism makes it difficult for South Asian actors to advance in the industry.
cards.body:
Ambika Mod, the British actress known for This Is Going To Hurt and Netflix's One Day, said she believes systemic racism in the entertainment industry makes it difficult for South Asian actors to advance. The 31-year-old told BBC Newsbeat that the glass ceiling for South Asian actors is "always getting higher and higher and higher."

Mod, who joins the cast of Black Doves for its second season, said she carefully selects roles and will not take parts she considers tokenistic or stereotypical. A Creative Diversity Network report found that representation of minority ethnic groups on and off-screen dropped slightly last year, while media watchdog Ofcom reported that people from minority ethnic groups account for only 11 percent of senior management roles in UK broadcasting.

cards.headline: Norris takes pole in rain-delayed Brazilian Grand Prix qualifying amid dangerous conditions
cards.teaser: McLaren driver Lando Norris secured pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after qualifying was halted for nearly 90 minutes due to extreme wet conditions that drivers called borderline dangerous.
cards.body:
Lando Norris claimed pole position for the Brazilian Grand Prix after qualifying was stopped for nearly 90 minutes when conditions were deemed too dangerous to continue. Norris, who described the session as among the wettest he had driven in, said his third consecutive pole in Brazil came because wet conditions compensated for McLaren lacking dry pace. George Russell, who qualified second, said drivers were aquaplaning at over 120 mph with zero visibility and called the conditions crazy, warning that racing in such weather risked a horrific incident.

Grid penalties for engine changes left Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen starting 20th and 21st. Norris and Russell both said they hope for rain in Sunday's race, believing wet conditions will give them better opportunities to make a difference.

cards.headline: Hutchinson beats Buatsi to win WBC light-heavyweight title
cards.teaser: Scottish boxer Willy Hutchinson won the WBC light-heavyweight championship in Manchester, avenging his 2024 loss to Joshua Buatsi.
cards.body:
Willy Hutchinson won the WBC light-heavyweight championship after defeating Joshua Buatsi in Manchester on Saturday. The 28-year-old Scottish boxer won by decision with judges scoring the bout 117-112, 115-113, and 115-113, avenging his loss to Buatsi in their 2024 fight. The contest was elevated from an interim title fight when American David Benavidez vacated the championship to move to cruiserweight.

Hutchinson became the eighth British light-heavyweight champion and the first since Nathan Cleverly in 2017. His record improved to 21 wins and two losses, while Buatsi suffered his second defeat in 22 professional fights. Hutchinson said winning the title fulfilled a childhood dream he wrote about at age 13.

cards.headline: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
cards.teaser: Gadi Eisenkot has 28 days to build a coalition after an election left no bloc with a Knesset majority.
cards.body:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government following last week's election, in which no bloc secured a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot, whose centrist Yashar party and allied opposition parties won 48 seats, received 67 recommendations for the premiership during Herzog's consultations, compared to 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose right-wing coalition won 53 seats.

Eisenkot has 28 days to assemble a government, with a potential 14-day extension. Two Arab-led alliances won an unprecedented 19 seats, positioning them as potential coalition partners, though most Jewish parties pledged before the election not to work with them. No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority.

cards.headline: Musk says SpaceX could buy legacy telecom carrier, use spectrum 'ten times more effectively'
cards.teaser: SpaceX CEO floated acquisition possibility at investment conference, while Deutsche Telekom CEO pegged entry cost at $220 billion.
cards.body:
Elon Musk told investors on November 6 that SpaceX could buy a legacy telecom carrier and use its airwaves "ten times more effectively," though he named no target and made any purchase conditional on better spectrum use. He spoke by video at the Baron Investment Conference in New York. SpaceX rose 8.62% to $134.27, while Verizon and AT&T each slipped 0.89%.

Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Hoettges said on November 5 that SpaceX would need at least $220 billion to compete with established U.S. carriers, citing SpaceX's 76 MHz of spectrum compared with roughly 400 MHz for T-Mobile. Any acquisition would also require taking on debt—Verizon holds $166.2 billion and AT&T $159.6 billion—along with antitrust and FCC approval.

cards.headline: U.S. intelligence memo says China recruited Megaspeed executive to spy on Nvidia CEO
cards.teaser: The memo claimed Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather intelligence on Jensen Huang.
cards.body:
A U.S. intelligence memo circulated earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports. The memo also alleged Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang.

An Nvidia spokesperson said Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were not unusual and that the company does not share classified information with customers. The New York Times first reported the existence of the memo.

cards.headline: Data center restrictions gain ground in midterm elections as voters reject ballot measures, elect skeptical leaders
cards.teaser: Voters rejected dozens of local ballot measures favoring data centers and elected officials who pledged restrictions, including Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa.
cards.body:
Voters in dozens of local jurisdictions rejected ballot measures related to data center expansion in this week's midterm elections, while electing officials who campaigned on restricting such facilities. In Texas, governor-elect Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott after promising to focus on data center restrictions. The ballot measures largely sought to impose restrictions or moratoriums on data centers, and most passed.

OpenAI responded by releasing what it calls a compute campus policy blueprint, pledging to end nondisclosure agreement requirements for local officials and increase transparency about project plans. The company is also attempting to rebrand data centers as compute campuses following growing opposition tied to environmental concerns, particularly water use in drought-prone regions.

cards.headline: U.S. intelligence memo alleges Chinese espionage targeting Nvidia CEO
cards.teaser: A circulated memo claimed a technology executive was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Jensen Huang.
cards.body:
A U.S. intelligence memo circulated earlier this year alleged that Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports. The memo also claimed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang.

An Nvidia spokesperson told The New York Times that Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were not unusual and that the company does not share classified information with customers. Separately, reporters investigating a Chinese company authorized to buy advanced Nvidia chips found only an empty shell at its listed office address, raising concerns it could be a front for a blacklisted firm.

cards.headline: Binance CFO departs weeks after $6.3 billion hack linked to North Korean group
cards.teaser: Kaiser Ng is leaving the cryptocurrency exchange to pursue a new venture, the company says, following a massive theft that prompted a multiday withdrawal freeze.
cards.body:
Kaiser Ng is leaving his role as chief financial officer at Binance to pursue a new venture after more than five years at the cryptocurrency exchange, co-CEO Yi He said in a statement. The announcement comes about a week after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance users in an attack that Binance and the FBI attributed to a North Korean group called TraderTraitor.

Binance froze withdrawals for several days following the hack. After accounts were unfrozen, users withdrew a net $3.6 billion in the first few hours. The company said it would cover all losses and not pass costs to users. Justin Yek will replace Ng as CFO.

cards.headline: Microsoft researcher John Langford exits, declares AI Frontiers group finished
cards.teaser: A veteran Microsoft researcher left the company after his research group was moved into a division he says prioritizes scaling over fundamental AI research.
cards.body:
John Langford, a partner researcher manager at Microsoft Research New York, left Microsoft and declared the AI Frontiers research group finished. The roughly 50-person group, which Langford founded in 2023 to pursue organized AI research following ChatGPT's release, was moved from Microsoft Research into Microsoft AI in early September.

Langford wrote on his blog that Microsoft AI leadership focuses on scaling rather than research, an approach he called misdirected. He said he could not get innovations used or seriously considered within Microsoft AI, and doubted research could reach application from Microsoft Research either. Langford placed remaining team members before departing.

cards.headline: Scientists identify two enormous tears in tectonic plate beneath Iran
cards.teaser: Researchers using seismic monitoring have discovered two converging ruptures in the Arabian Plate, offering rare insight into how oceans close and continents collide.
cards.body:
Researchers led by a team from the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified two large tears in the Arabian Plate beneath southeastern Iran, caused by differences in rock density between oceanic and continental portions of the plate. Using data from 69 seismic monitoring stations collected between March 2017 and September 2018, the team found one horizontal tear where the Zagros collision zone meets the Makran subduction zone, and a smaller vertical tear near the Makran Trench.

The tears, which have been progressing for several million years, are expected to eventually merge as they advance. The findings, published in Nature Geoscience, provide scientists with a rare look at the transition from oceanic subduction to continental collision and the final stages of the ancient Neo-Tethys Ocean's closure.

cards.headline: Companies roll out child-focused phones and monitoring devices as parents seek safer alternatives to smartphones
cards.teaser: Devices like Bark Phone, Gabb, and Pinwheel offer restricted features, parental controls, and content monitoring in response to growing concerns over unrestricted smartphone access for children.
cards.body:
A growing number of companies are developing phones and devices specifically designed for children as parents express concern about unrestricted smartphone access. Products like Bark Phone, Gabb, and Pinwheel typically feature touchscreens and cameras but restrict or remove web browsers, social media, and app stores. Parents can manage devices through companion apps to approve contacts, monitor locations, set screen time limits, and receive alerts about potential online dangers.

Some companies offer minimalist approaches, including calling-and-texting-only phones or home devices like Tin Can and Pinwheel Home. Pricing varies widely, with devices ranging from around $68 to $240 and monthly service fees starting between $7.99 and $35. Several products, including Waffle and TextNow's recent entry, allow parents to gradually unlock features as children mature.

hero.headline: Willy Hutchinson upsets Joshua Buatsi to win WBC light-heavyweight title in Manchester rematch
hero.body:
Willy Hutchinson won the WBC light-heavyweight championship Saturday night in Manchester, defeating Joshua Buatsi by decision to avenge a loss from 2024. The judges scored the rematch 117-112, 115-113, 115-113 in favor of Hutchinson, making the 28-year-old Scot the first British champion at the weight since Nathan Cleverly in 2017. The bout was elevated from an interim title fight to a full championship after American David Benavidez vacated the belt to move up to cruiserweight.

Hutchinson, who said he wrote about his dream of becoming a WBC champion at age 13, delivered what he called a mature performance after losing to Buatsi in their first meeting. In 2024, Buatsi had sent Hutchinson to the canvas twice with body shots, but this time Hutchinson had answers for the Londoner's strategy. He controlled the center of the ring, landed rapid triple jabs, and switched stances to outbox his opponent before a vocal Manchester crowd at the AO Arena.

An emotional Hutchinson dedicated the victory to his coach after the decision was announced. "Without him I don't think I'll be here today let alone boxing," Hutchinson said. "This man dug me out of a hole that I never thought that I would get out of, so this is all a bonus baby." The win improved his record to 21 victories and two defeats, while Buatsi suffered his second loss in 22 professional fights.

Hutchinson immediately called out former world title challenger Anthony Yarde, who was ringside and entered the ring after the fight. A potential unification bout could also emerge depending on the outcome of the December 12 fight between Dmitry Bivol and Callum Smith for the other three light-heavyweight titles. Domestic rival Ben Whittaker, who holds the WBC silver title, is another possible opponent.

cards.headline: Chris Billam-Smith stopped for first time as Chev Clarke wins with seventh-round knockdowns
cards.teaser: The former cruiserweight world champion was knocked down twice in the seventh round before the referee intervened in their all-British non-title fight.
cards.body:
Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith was knocked down and stopped for the first time in his career as Chev Clarke won their all-British non-title fight Saturday. Clarke landed a right hand at the start of the seventh round, and although Billam-Smith beat the count, he was down again moments later after a barrage of punches. The referee stopped the contest after Clarke connected with two more blows, with Billam-Smith immediately protesting the decision.

The loss was the third professional defeat for Billam-Smith, who previously lost to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and Richard Riakporhe in 2019. Clarke, who also beat Billam-Smith in the amateur ranks a decade ago, improved to 13 wins and two defeats.

cards.headline: Norris takes pole for Sao Paulo Grand Prix in wet qualifying as Hamilton and Verstappen start from back
cards.teaser: McLaren driver secures third consecutive Brazil pole in treacherous conditions delayed nearly 90 minutes, while engine penalties send champions to rear of grid.
cards.body:
Lando Norris claimed pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after qualifying in extreme wet conditions that forced a nearly 90-minute delay. The McLaren driver said the session brought some of the wettest conditions he had ever experienced, with Mercedes driver George Russell describing visibility as zero and aquaplaning at over 120 mph.

Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen will start 20th and 21st after taking engine penalties for exceeding their season allowances. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc qualified fourth but receives a 10-place penalty for engine usage. Light rain is forecast for Sunday's race at Interlagos.

cards.headline: Vikings linked to Colts quarterback Daniel Jones and running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of trade deadline
cards.teaser: Minnesota has emerged as a potential trade partner for Indianapolis, with interest in acquiring both players in a package deal.
cards.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have been linked to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and quarterback Daniel Jones as the NFL trade deadline approaches. Minnesota's interest in both players increased after quarterback Kyler Murray's performance in a 19-15 loss to Detroit, while the team's running game has also struggled.

A package deal could allow the Colts to secure a first-round pick, which Indianapolis would not receive by trading Taylor alone. The Vikings' running backs combined for just 42 yards on 13 carries in the Detroit loss, with Jordan Mason gaining 20 yards and Aaron Jones adding 22 yards.

cards.headline: BBC commentator calls FA Cup fog tie 'worst conditions in 35-year career'
cards.teaser: Steve Bower could barely see the pitch as thick fog enveloped Altrincham's ground during a live televised first-round match.
cards.body:
BBC Sport commentator Steve Bower described an FA Cup first-round tie between Altrincham and Notts County on Saturday as the most challenging broadcast of his 35-year career after thick fog made the pitch nearly invisible. Bower said that after the 60th minute, he could not see which team or player had the ball once play moved beyond the center circle, forcing him to rely on crowd reactions and replays to call the action.

The fog affected everyone at the Moss Lane ground. Managers could not assess tactical changes, players abandoned long passes because they could not see, and radio commentators admitted they did not know where the ball was. Notts County won on penalties after extra time, with Altrincham fans using phone lights to distract penalty takers in the fog.

cards.headline: Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson faces uncertain future after 4-0 home loss to last-place Hibernian
cards.teaser: Robinson vowed to keep fighting as manager after the defeat left Aberdeen in the relegation playoff position.
cards.body:
Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson said he will keep fighting until told otherwise after his team lost 4-0 at home to bottom-of-table Hibernian. The defeat, which Robinson called unacceptable, left Aberdeen in the relegation playoff position with four losses in their past five Scottish Premiership matches. Home fans booed and chanted "You're getting sacked in the morning" as Robinson left the field.

Robinson has won six of 21 league matches since taking over in March. The manager had labeled the match against Hibernian a must-win before the game. Aberdeen has now lost four consecutive matches across all competitions and has scored only three goals in their past six home league games.

cards.headline: No. 9 BYU meets Utah in first top-10 Holy War matchup, drawing national ABC broadcast
cards.teaser: No. 9 BYU will face Utah at Rice-Eccles Stadium in the first top-10 clash in the rivalry's history, with millions expected to watch on ABC. The game represents a transformation for
cards.body:
No. 9 BYU will face Utah at Rice-Eccles Stadium in the first top-10 clash in the rivalry's history, with millions expected to watch on ABC. The game represents a transformation for

The game represents a transformation for what was once a regional grudge match into must-see television for college football fans nationwide. The rivalry has drawn increasing national attention since Utah joined the Pac-12 in 2011 and BYU went independent with an ESPN deal for its home games.

hero.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero heads toward $32 million opening weekend, surpassing predecessor's total domestic run
hero.body:
Godzilla Minus Zero is tracking toward a $32 million domestic box office debut, far exceeding the full theatrical run of its 2023 predecessor. The sequel, which centers on postwar Japan dealing with attacks from the three-headed Ghidorah and the possibility of Godzilla's return, is outpacing Godzilla Minus One, which opened in December 2023 with $11.4 million and finished its domestic run at $57.1 million.

The film holds a 90 percent critics approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The Hollywood Reporter chief film critic David Rooney called it a thrilling jolt of marauding monster action. Godzilla Minus One became Japan's first feature to win the Academy Award for best visual effects, adding $56.9 million internationally to its domestic total.

Warner Bros.' The Cat in the Hat opened in second place with $6 million domestically on Friday, including Thursday previews, from 4,003 North American locations. The animated film is projected to reach around $18 million for its opening weekend. The studio had initially projected a $20 million opening for the $92 million production and is hoping word of mouth will sustain the film through the Thanksgiving holiday and into December.

The Cat in the Hat, directed by Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni, earned an A CinemaScore from opening-weekend audiences. The film is an animated adaptation of the Dr. Seuss book.

cards.headline: Sylvester Stallone says rivalry with Arnold Schwarzenegger ended when Schwarzenegger ran for California governor
cards.teaser: The action star recounts their decades-long competition and why it cooled only after Schwarzenegger left acting for politics.
cards.body:
Sylvester Stallone said his rivalry with Arnold Schwarzenegger lasted 20 years and ended only when Schwarzenegger ran for California governor. In a recent podcast interview, Stallone described the competition as contentious, with both actors vying to lead the action genre through films like "Rambo" and "Commando." The tension persisted even after they partnered on the restaurant chain Planet Hollywood in 1991.

Stallone said the rivalry cooled when Schwarzenegger stopped making movies to pursue politics. The two remain friendly, though Stallone noted they are still competitive by nature but no longer financially.

cards.headline: AI filmmaking could surpass 35mm costs as token fees rise, Korean producers warn
cards.teaser: Studio executives caution that runaway token costs and piecemeal revisions risk making AI production more expensive than celluloid-era filmmaking.
cards.body:
Kim Kwang-jib, CEO of Korean AI studio Studio Meta-K, told Taiwan Creative Content Fest that token costs for a 100-minute film can reach 500 million won, or roughly $366,000, using current commercial tools. If AI companies raise token prices tenfold as they seek profitability, costs could hit 5 billion won and exceed typical Asian feature budgets, he said.

Kim compared the economics to the 35mm era, when meticulous preproduction limited costly film stock usage. With AI, every revision requires a new paid render, and clients submitting changes one at a time over multiple days can multiply costs. Unless preproduction is rigorous, he said, AI could spend more than 35mm filmmaking.

cards.headline: Pokemon anime studio unveils AI coloring tool trained on three hand-painted frames
cards.teaser: OLM developed the system under a Japan government-backed research project, estimating it has cut painting workload by around 30 percent.
cards.body:
OLM developed the system under a Japan government-backed research project, estimating it has cut painting workload by around 30 percent.

OLM, the Japanese animation studio behind the Pokemon anime series and films, has developed an AI coloring tool that learns a show's visual style from just three hand-painted frames, OLM Digital board director Yotsukura Tatsuo said at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest in Taipei. The tool emerged from ANIMINS, a 15-month research project led by Yotsukura under GENIAC, a generative AI program overseen by Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry that concluded in February.

cards.headline: Animator Sylvain Chomet denies AI use in Dior ad, cites automated interpolation tool
cards.teaser: The Oscar-nominated director responded to viral speculation about generative AI in the luxury brand's holiday campaign, which was promoted as hand-drawn.
cards.body:
Four-time Oscar-nominated French director Sylvain Chomet denied that generative artificial intelligence was used in a holiday advertising campaign he created for luxury fashion brand Dior, which the company had promoted as hand-drawn animation. Chomet and producer Aton Soumache told Variety that a team of 20 artists worked on the ad over seven months, but acknowledged using what Soumache called "an automated interpolation system for a very small part of the process."

The filmmakers did not identify the software or explain how the interpolation tool worked. Viral online speculation about possible AI use focused on visual anomalies including extra fingers and morphing objects in the finished animation. Chomet attributed those elements to established hand-drawn animation techniques involving exaggerated shapes to convey movement.

cards.headline: Papua New Guinea's most expensive film wraps after 40-day shoot
cards.teaser: The $4.5 million drama Mussau: The First Song completed principal photography across two provinces, with producers hoping for an Oscar submission.
cards.body:
The $4.5 million drama Mussau: The First Song completed principal photography across two provinces, with producers hoping for an Oscar submission.

Papua New Guinea's most expensive film to date, the $4.5 million historical drama Mussau: The First Song, has wrapped principal photography after a 40-day shoot across two provinces. Filming took place on Mussau Island in New Ireland Province and in Goroka, in Eastern Highlands Province.

cards.headline: Eleven artists compete for Best New Artist at 2026 Latin Grammys
cards.teaser: The ceremony takes place Nov. 12 in Las Vegas, with nominees including Colombian artist Aria Vega and Mexican-American singer Delilah.
cards.body:
Eleven artists from Latin America, the United States, and Spain are competing for Best New Artist at the 2026 Latin Grammys, which takes place Nov. 12 in Las Vegas. Past winners of the award include Calle 13, Karol G, and Silvana Estrada.

Four of this year's nominees described their paths to the nomination. Colombian artist Aria Vega said the recognition represents Barranquilla and the Caribbean coast. Mexican-American singer Delilah, who opened twice for Natanael Cano at Mexico City's Estadio GNP Seguros, said representing women in música mexicana is meaningful. Peruvian artist Fabian, whose sister Nicole was nominated in 2022, is working on a debut album. Mexican-Swedish artist Sofia Monroy was nominated for her album Morena.

hero.headline: Congress demands answers on Nvidia CEO's reported ties to alleged Chinese spy
hero.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing congressional scrutiny after reports surfaced that he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Sen. Chris Coons pledged an investigation, while a group of House Republican committee chairs requested a briefing from Huang by November 11 to determine whether U.S. national security has been compromised.

Multiple news outlets reported Friday that Alice Huang, a tech executive with whom Jensen Huang had contact, was recruited by Chinese intelligence officials to influence the Nvidia CEO's position on U.S. chip export policy toward China. The New York Times and Financial Times reported she was specifically tasked with convincing him to lobby U.S. officials to allow exports of advanced chips to China. The Financial Times also reported that the two had a romantic relationship.

Nvidia has denied that Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang was anything beyond a typical business contact and said no sensitive information was shared. The Chinese government has also denied involvement. The company did not respond to a request for comment Saturday.

The House Republican chairs who requested the briefing asked Huang to explain his relationship with Alice Huang and detail Nvidia's controls over sensitive information. Nvidia produces chips central to advanced artificial intelligence development, a technology priority for the Trump administration as it seeks to maintain a competitive edge over China. Reports indicate Nvidia chips have reached Chinese companies despite export restrictions.

cards.headline: Trump replaces chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller after GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'
cards.body:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'

Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night after Trump blamed her for the election results in which Republicans lost control of Congress. Trump will install Miller, currently deputy chief of staff, in the position starting Monday.
